summary: In Greek mythology, Autesion (Ancient Greek Αὐτεσίων) is a king of Thebes, son of Tisamenus and descendant of Polynices. At an oracle's command he leaves Thebes for the Peloponnese among the Dorians; through his daughter Argeia he is grandfather of the Spartan twin kings Eurysthenes and Procles.
etymology: Greek Αὐτεσίων; Pausanias ties his departure to the Furies of Laius and Oedipus still haunting the Cadmean house.

sections.heading: From Thebes to the Dorians
paragraphs: Apollodorus, Pausanias, Herodotus, and Strabo know Autesion as son of Tisamenus, grandson of Thersander, and great-grandson of Polynices and Argia. He succeeds at Thebes, then — by oracle — migrates to join the Dorians in the Peloponnese. Pausanias says the Erinyes of Laius and Oedipus at last vented their wrath on him.

His children include Theras and Argeia; by Argeia, Aristodemus fathers Eurysthenes and Procles, the twin founders of the dual Spartan kingship. Nonnus also uses the name for a warrior slain in the Dionysiaca — a separate figure.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id autesion-theban is the Theban–Dorian king alone, not Nonnus' Indian-war casualty.
